- When sentiment is high (≥0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment periods.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d horizon, especially after a recent spike; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment history shows a sharp rise followed by decline, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% for 2–3 days post-sentiment peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in late 30d horizon (days 20–30); if forecast is above 70, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence to recent 10-day average.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low (≤0.1) and price is trending down; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment is low and price is falling.
